title: Lesson 50 - Can We Clarify the Brief?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Can we clarify the brief before I revise the layout? Priya's note says, “Make it friendly, include everything volunteers need and keep it short.”

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Yes. We don't know whether “volunteers” means only the opening-hour greeters or everyone working that day.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Could you confirm who the primary audience is? That's question one.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: We also need the delivery format. Do they want a one-page PDF, a mobile page or both?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Question two: could you confirm whether the final deliverable is a mobile-friendly one-page PDF?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: And “everything they need” could become unlimited. When you say must-have information, do you mean arrival time, entrance, station, break handoff and contact chain?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That's question three. I also need to know what “short” means.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Ask for a page or word limit rather than guessing.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Question four: is there a maximum length we should work to?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: The last gap is approval. Who has final approval, and who only verifies logistics?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Priya has replied. The audience is only the opening-hour greeters.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: What format did she confirm?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: One mobile-friendly PDF, one page, ideally under three hundred words.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: And the must-haves?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Arrival time, accessible entrance, service-desk station, break handoff and a role-based contact chain. No exhibition content or personal phone numbers.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Who signs off?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Priya has final content approval. Sam verifies access and facilities details; he doesn't approve the whole document.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Let me make sure I've got this right. The brief is a one-page internal PDF for opening-hour greeters, under three hundred words, with five operational sections. Priya approves it, and Sam checks only logistics.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Exactly. The internal-review deadline is still Thursday at four; public distribution isn't part of this task.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I see your point about stating that boundary. If anyone needs more than the internal sheet, we'll need a separate brief.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Good. Now I can revise the right document instead of making an attractive answer to the wrong question.
